newsitem.title: USA: U.S. prescription prices seen up under 2 pct in 96.
newsitem.headline: U.S. prescription prices seen up under 2 pct in 96.

text.p: Overall prescription drug prices in the United States are estimated to rise less than two percent in 1996 versus last year, according to an IMS America report released on Thursday.
In 1995, these prices rose 1.7 percent, it said.
IMS, a unit of Cognizant Corp, provides U.S. pharmaceutical sales and marketing information.
It said the projected pricing increase was based on data gathered for the first three quarters of 1996.

Robert Merold, vice president of marketing at IMS, said: "Our databases have shown overall increases for the first, second and third quarters of 1.3 percent, 1.8 percent and two percent, respectively."
IMS data was based on a list of products and actual transaction prices, rather than list prices, it said. Transaction prices are those the purchaser pays the manufacturer.
